newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases to 13.0/14.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases to 13.0/14.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged down to 13.0/14.0 percent from a high of 20.0 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers said liquidity appeared to be tight at the opening following a neutral central bank money policy.
They said, however, liquidity eased in mid-morning, driving overnight rates lower along with longer-term money.
One local bank dealer said the market was volatile, with overnight money opening at 13.5/15.0 percent and trending up before cooling off in the late morning.
One state bank dealer said money withdrawn from banks at month-end had not returned to the system, causing a temporary squeeze which could ease later.
The local bank dealer said operators remained cautious over a possible repeat of Monday's condition swhen overnight rates jumped in the afternoon due to a delay in clearing trades.
Another said the market was mixed in assessing the short-term outlook as liquidity was tight in the early part of the month.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates stable, offering one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 17.69 percent, compared with 12.16 percent on Friday.
One bond dealer said interest remained firm on good corporate issues but appeared to soften on paper issued by property companies.
